**Verdict on the pre-written rule (README section 3): DISAGREE.**

- Rule 1, flat plate: SM = 1.0% MAC (need 3 to 25%): NOT MET
- Rule 2: 7 of 15 curl configurations trim about the CG at a CL between 0.2 and 0.9
- Rule 1, every trimming curl: SM from 1.0 to 1.0% MAC: NOT MET

## How big is the DISAGREE: inside drawing resolution

The neutral point is 0.31 mm behind the marked cross; the rule's floor (3% of MAC) is 0.98 mm (about 1 mm); the traced outline's two halves differ by 0.31 mm rms; one scan pixel is 0.08 mm; the neutral point moves by at most 0.03 mm with the AVL section count. **It is not evidence that the published mark or the model is wrong.** Candidate explanations, none tested here:

- (i) the hand-drawn CG cross is approximate (its two strokes are a few tenths of a millimetre wide and the drawing's two halves differ by about the same);
- (ii) AVL's neutral point for a low-aspect-ratio swept flat plate: plate_balance suggests the real aerodynamic centre is 0 to 5% of the MAC ahead of AVL's, which alone is 0 to 1.6 mm at this size;
- (iii) the published glider is probably near-neutral and forgiving at its very low wing loading (about 1.7 N/m2), so it need not have a 3% margin to fly;
- (iv) the real foam plate is several millimetres thick on a 37 mm chord, which the flat-plate model ignores;
- (v) the real curl may be camber or dihedral rather than twist: that changes the trim, not the neutral point.

The forward CGs are model-based and Kai's choice: a margin of about 1% is where the pull-out model cannot say, and measured plates put the aerodynamic centre ahead of AVL's, so the real margin at each CG is uncertain by about the size of the shifts tried. The knife-edge balance on the real part is what counts.

## A PLA print is not the known-good design

The printed plate shares the outline only (first step of the morph). Wing loading 12.4 N/m2 (PLA 0.6 mm) or 6.0 (LW-PLA 0.6 g/cm3) against 1.7 for the foam original (100 g/m2 ASSUMED): at CL 0.45 about 2.7 times the speed and about 7 times the first-swoop depth for PLA. The true baseline is a foam-plate replica at the published loading.
